items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: Well in a sense we did because we were immersed in the music of King Oliver, Jelly Roll Morton, Armstrong Hot Five, and we wanted to play in that style.

ctx.x: Did you know you were doing revival at the time?

Well in a sense we did because we were immersed in the music of King Oliver, Jelly Roll Morton, Armstrong Hot Five, and we wanted to play in that style. We didn’t want to imitate their records. We wanted to play in their style but be creative at the same time. And yeah, in a sense it was quite different from the traditional jazz that was happening around New York at that time. I mean that was mostly centered around the Eddie Condon group and Pee Wee Russell and those guys, who were doing their own thing but it…
Is it possible to put into words what was different about the Condon style and the style that you were emulating?
